consumes.mechanism: contract client over the published API of tenant_authority, executed in process at Level 0
consumes.credential_source: deployment secret resolved by the composition root: the service identity of the consuming component
consumes.assembled_by: composition root or test fixture; identity's HTTP module composes nothing and publishes no object of tenant_authority
consumes.note: Tenant state and ownership are read from the authority at the authorization boundary; the effective tenant id is still derived only from verified identity. The client is value-only and is bound to this component's own service identity: identity receives no engine, store, audit journal or mutation operation, and cannot choose the actor recorded in the authority's journal. Identity's published HTTP surface (`identity_service.api`) serves only its own API: the authority's contract application is not owned or re-exported by it. A Tenant of another Platform Instance is answered as unknown, so identity reports TENANT_UNKNOWN while the authority keeps the precise ownership denial. The client is value-only down to its own state — an opaque contract channel handle, a credential and a Platform Instance binding — so identity holds neither the authority's ASGI application nor a transport object that could reach it.

operations.purpose: verified identity of the presented credential
verified subject and effective tenant of the request; grants nothing

consumer_surface.published_by: identity_service.reader.build_client (called by the composition root with this component's own contract application)
consumer_surface.transport: identity_service.transport.open_channel + identity_service.transport.call_contract — the published HTTP contract executed in process over an opaque channel handle (ARCHITECTURE.md §1.1 interaction mode API, Level 0)
errors: identity_service.errors.AccessDenied — reconstructed from status code and machine-readable reason
identity_service.errors.ContractViolation — raised when the component answers outside its contract; a consumer must fail closed
guarantees: values only: no store handle, audit journal, idempotency table, engine reference or record operation is reachable through the published surface
the published client holds no callable and no credential of its own: the subject credential is presented per call, exactly as over HTTP
the ASGI application is never handed out: it stays behind the provider-side channel table, and a channel is revoked when the consumer drops the client
the answer is a context, never a grant: it carries no permission list and no tenant lifecycle state
consumer_surface.note: The context read publishes the effective tenant derived from the verified identity, so a consuming component (IS-003) does not need — and cannot build — a second tenant-context mechanism.

events.note: IS-001 does not publish inter-component events. Audit is an internal immutable log owned by identity, not a public event contract.

data_export_cdc.note: No CDC/export stream is implemented in IS-001. Audit remains internal owned data.

ui.note: Class B Platform Service; no product UI in IS-001.

current_platform_id.description: Platform Instance this identity boundary serves; ownership of a Tenant is verified against it.

notes: Identity owns identity and association data only. Tenant lifecycle state and Platform Instance ownership are owned by Tenant Authority (IS-002) and are read through its published contract, never copied here (invariant T-004).

authn.note: IS-001 proves verification boundary; it is not a full IAM product.

authz.authorization_authority: authorization (IS-003) decides ALLOW/DENY for platform consumers; identity keeps enforcing its own records at its own boundary (ARCHITECTURE.md §6.2)

changelog.change: Additive: published context read GET /api/v1/context and the value-only consumer surface identity_service.reader.IdentityContextClient, so that IS-003 (Authorization Boundary) obtains the verified subject and the effective tenant from this component instead of inventing a second identity or tenant-context mechanism. No existing operation changed; nothing new is granted by the addition.

IS-002 integration: Tenant lifecycle state and Platform Instance ownership are read from Tenant Authority; the local tenant registry copy and a second Tenant state vocabulary were removed. Public API /api/v1 is unchanged (additive observability context fields only).
